# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.19 (pre-release)

Changes since pre.18 (2 fixes) plus a **verified user guide** attached to the release. Everything was written and tested by the author's assistant on one Linux machine; **nothing was tried on Windows, macOS or arm64, and the GUI was not re-tried in a window after these two fixes.**

**Fixes**
- **Automatic sideways check no longer turns picture pages.** On a page that is mostly a photograph with vertical ornaments (page 15 of the tester's PDF) the built-in check turned the page by 90° although the original was upright (reproduced on Linux, in the command line and in the window). Borderline evidence is now left alone: the columns must beat the rows by a factor of 4 unless the line structure is strong. A text page lying on its side is still turned upright (tested). Pages that are borderline are not turned by the built-in check any more; Tesseract's orientation (OSD) and the manual rotate buttons are unchanged. Not measured on the large book corpus of earlier editions (not available in this session).
- **`--save-project` keeps `--work-area` and `--cut-at`.** In pre.18 a project saved from the command line lost these two global values; they are now written as `work_area =` and `cut_at =` and read back (round trip tested; a saved project reopened with `--project` gave the same pages and text).

**Guide**
- `LegatorOCR-0.2.0-pre.19-ghid.pdf` (Romanian, 26 pages A4, 34 screenshots). Every command in it was run on pre.18/pre.19 test data, and the GUI parts were tried in a real window on Linux. Corrections made while verifying: `--redact` presets, `--fuse-frames` takes an output file, five kinds of drawing zones. The guide lists what was NOT verified (Windows/macOS/arm64, corner resize of zones, native file dialogs, PDF/UA, CIUS-RO, veraPDF).

**Known limits (unchanged)**: Windows, macOS and arm64 builds are untested by the author; OCR can misread characters such as `@`, so redaction results must be checked by eye; the rotation behaviour reported on Windows 11 is unconfirmed.
